html:
The Saramaka are a Maroon people of Suriname, descended from Africans who escaped the plantations and built free villages in the rainforest. In 1762 they won a peace treaty with the Dutch, two years after the Ndyuka.

Escape from the brutal sugar plantations was common from the 1600s. The runaways settled deep upriver, kept African ways of farming, religion and art, and raided the plantations. The Dutch could not defeat them, and in the treaties of 1760 and 1762 recognised their freedom in return for a promise to return new runaways.

The Maroons of Suriname are the largest such communities in the Americas. Their villages were flooded by the Brokopondo dam in the 1960s, and in 2007 the Saramaka won a case at the Inter-American Court over their land rights in Suriname.
